title: Clamp a thermometer on the suction line near its service valve and insulate it
instruction: Mount the blue pipe-clamp thermometer on the suction line: set it astride the line, on bare copper with its middle within 15 cm of the suction service valve's body and clear of the brazed joint next to the valve. Then set the black foam cover over the clamp to insulate it, and let go of both.
context: HVAC mechanics and installers (O*NET 49-9021.00: 'inspect and test systems ... to detect and locate malfunctions') check an air conditioner's refrigerant charge by superheat on fixed-orifice systems. Superheat needs the suction-line temperature, read by a clamp-on thermometer. Bryant's split-system service instructions (superheat charging method): 'Measure vapor-line temperature by attaching a service thermometer to unit vapor line near vapor valve.' and 'Insulate thermometer for accurate readings.' The suction (vapour) line is the larger of the two copper lines at the condensing unit and is normally insulated; the small bare one is the liquid line. A clamp on the liquid line, on a fitting, on the foam or far down the line, or left uncovered, reads the wrong temperature and the charge is set wrong. Here 'near' is taken as within 15 cm (6 in), a figure from technician guides, not a maker's rule.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the table: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. Everything is fixed except the clamp and the cover; every block is square to x and y. (1) Condensing-unit corner: a grey painted steel box 12 (x) x 6 (y) x 16 cm tall, x 23 to 35, y 22 to 28. (2) Suction service valve: a brass block, a 3 cm cube, centred at x 25, y 20.5, 7 cm up, against the unit's right (-y) face; its body face toward the line is at y 19. A brass port cap, a cylinder 1 cm across and 1 cm tall, stands on its top. (3) Liquid service valve: a brass block, a 2.4 cm cube, centred at x 32, y 20.8, 6.53 cm up, against the same face, with a brass port cap 0.8 cm across and 0.8 cm tall on top. (4) Suction line, along y, its axis at x 25, 7 cm up: from the valve's face a brazed coupling, a darker brazed-copper block 2.5 x 2.5 cm in section, to y 16.5 (top 8.25 cm up); then bare copper, a copper bar 1.9 x 1.9 cm in section (the width of 3/4 in tube), from y 16.5 to y -8 (top 7.95 cm up); then black closed-cell foam insulation, a block 4.5 x 4.5 cm in section, from y -8 to y -15. (5) Liquid line: a copper bar 0.95 x 0.95 cm in section (3/8 in tube) along y, its axis at x 32, 6.53 cm up, from the liquid valve's face (y 19.6) to y -15. (6) Two grey painted wooden blocks from y -13.5 to -10.5 hold the lines up: x 22.75 to 27.25 and 4.75 cm tall under the foam; x 31 to 33 and 6.05 cm tall under the liquid line. (7) Two grey start pads, plastic plates 0.3 cm thick: 8 x 8 cm centred at x 15, y 20, and 9 x 9 cm centred at x 15, y 8.5. (8) Thermometer clamp, loose, 60 g, blue anodised aluminium: a saddle made of a top block 4.9 (x) x 4 (y) x 1.6 cm with a black plastic display 2.4 (x) x 2 (y) x 0.4 cm centred on its top, and two legs 0.8 (x) x 4 (y) x 2 cm under its two x edges, along its full 4 cm length, 3.3 cm apart inside: the legs pass 7 mm either side of the 1.9 cm suction line while the block's underside rests on the copper's top. It stands on its legs on the 8 x 8 cm pad, centred at x 15, y 20, legs along y, display up. (9) Insulation cover, loose, 20 g, black closed-cell foam: a half-shell 7.7 (x) x 7 (y) x 4.6 cm, a roof 7.7 x 7 x 1 cm on two walls 0.6 (x) x 7 (y) x 3.6 cm under its x edges, leaving a channel along y 6.5 cm wide and 3.6 cm high (8 mm either side of the clamp; set over the clamp, its ceiling rests on the display). It stands on its walls on the 9 x 9 cm pad, centred at x 15, y 8.5, channel along y. Nothing else is on the table. The layout is the same in every trial.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial; the run ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s. Terms. At rest: the part moved less than 3 mm in all over the last 0.5 s. The clamp's centre is the centre of its top block's underside. Seated: the clamp is astride the bare copper of the suction line: its centre within 8 mm of the line's axis (x 25) across the line and from 1 mm below to 2 mm above the copper's top (7.95 cm up), so the underside rests on the copper with a leg either side; tilted at most 4 degrees; its legs within 20 degrees of the line's direction, either way round; the whole block over bare copper (all four corners of its underside between y 16.5, the coupling's end, and y -8, the foam's end); and at rest. Resting astride, the legs leave 7 mm of play a side and cannot turn past about 18 degrees, so the 8 mm and 20 degree limits never fail a clamp that rests astride. A clamp on the coupling (3 mm higher) or the foam, on a valve, on the liquid line, on the table or a pad, or turned across the line on its legs, is not seated. d: the distance along the line from the suction valve's body face (y 19) to the clamp's centre (its middle, not its near end); a seated clamp has d from 4.5 to 25 cm. Insulated: seen from above, the four top corners of the clamp's block lie inside the cover's 7.7 x 7 cm outline (in the cover's own frame); the cover's channel ceiling, at its centre, is from 1 mm below to 3 mm above the top of the clamp's display (resting on it); the cover is tilted at most 10 degrees; and it is at rest. Clear of a part: each gripper's tool point and the point between its finger tips are both at least 4 cm above the top of the box around that part, or both at least 6.5 cm from that box seen from above (an open finger reaches 5.7 cm to the side of the tool point). Scores. 1.0 if the clamp is seated with d at most 15 cm and insulated, and both grippers are clear of both parts. Otherwise, with both grippers clear of the clamp: 0.5 if the clamp is seated with d at most 15 cm (not insulated, or a gripper not yet clear of the cover); 0.25 if it is seated with d over 15 cm (insulated or not). 0 in every other case (a gripper not clear of the clamp; the clamp on the liquid line, the coupling, the foam, a valve, the table or a pad, tilted or moving; the cover alone; nothing done). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. A real trial is scored with a ruler and a top photo: d from the valve face to the clamp's middle; the clamp's legs either side of the bare copper and no part of it over the coupling or the foam; its block resting on the copper (no visible gap under its middle); the cover resting on the clamp with the whole block hidden under it from above; each gripper's finger tips at least 4 cm above both parts or at least 6.5 cm from them seen from above (from the clamp only, for 0.5 and 0.25).
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's uniform friction. The unit, valves, lines and foam are fixed. The copper lines are square bars as wide as the tubes, so the rigid clamp sits level on top (a real clamp's spring jaws centre it on the round tube), and the clamp rests by its weight instead of gripping. The cover is a rigid foam half-shell. No refrigerant, temperature, sun or wind is simulated: the score is the mounting a technician checks before reading the superheat.
reset_notes: Stand the clamp on its legs on its pad at x 15, y 20, legs along y, display up; stand the cover on its walls on its pad at x 15, y 8.5, channel along y. Nothing else moves or is consumed.
